craft_claim: Direct address to a reader ('you', apostrophe, or a letter frame) constitutes a para-social dyad that manufactures felt intimacy at a distance.

supporting_evidence.location: Psychiatry 19(3): 215-229, thesis of 'intimacy at a distance'
supporting_evidence.note: Media personae generate a sensed conversational friendship with the audience through address and apparent self-reference.
Apostrophe constitutes an addressee and forces writer and reader into an altered circuit of communication, making the address an event rather than a description.

supporting_evidence.location: Computers in Human Behavior 134: 107330, Studies 1 and 2
supporting_evidence.note: A performer's intimate self-disclosure raised perceived authenticity and liking, which increased acceptance of the performer's message.

scope: Lyric, blog/marketing copy, fiction, letters, and first-person nonfiction.
exceptions: Third-person narration can simulate intimacy via free indirect style without explicit address; see clm-tone-intimate-free-indirect-consciousness.
